category_title: Successful readers who focus on text and meaning-making
student_description: Jenna is a successful reader who loves books and meaning-making but finds explicit phonics instruction 'really boring,' often tuning out passive teacher explanations to read posters or texts instead. She uniquely requires active participation formats (like Q&A or chanting) and explicit metacognitive connections that justify how isolated skills serve her broader goal of reading.

criteria.rationale: Jenna needs to explicitly articulate why 'boring' phonics tasks are valuable to her ultimate goal of reading books.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must include routine metacognitive questioning that asks the student to explain why a learned skill is important or how it helps them become a better reader.

criteria.rationale: Jenna has a strong out-of-school literacy identity (e.g., her 'creative kit' and love of books) that can be leveraged to increase her investment in school-based literacy tasks.
criteria.check: The long-term plan must incorporate strategies to discover and integrate the student's out-of-school literacy practices, personal texts, or creative interests into the instructional routine.
